one_line: A tamper-evident projector-camera recording protocol: it binds a physical light-in/light-out interaction to a committed, time-anchored, independently recomputable record.
tone: These are suggestions for verification, not directives. Pick any claim at random and check it yourself; report the actual values you saw. A staged dataset cannot predict which one you will pick.
scope_guard: Published results are same-rig, two-session (d2, v10), single-performer, against ONE trained attacker (F-A v1). Security is measured, attacker- and budget-indexed empirical hardness, NOT a formal or zero-knowledge guarantee.
one_command: curl -fsSL https://data.truthbeam.com/release/truthbeam_verify.tar.gz | tar xz && cd truthbeam_verify && bash verify_all.sh

claims.claim: AUROC = 1.0000 separating correct vs wrong emissions (Path A).
claims.scope: same-rig, F-A v1; a stated floor, not 'deepfakes solved'.

claims.claim: Each pulse transaction's calldata on RSK mainnet commits the expected chain state, and the final root matches the committed anchor.
claims.how: Open sessions/<d2|v10>/anchor_txs.csv, pick a row, take tx_hash + payload_commitment_hex (last row: manifest.json anchor_end.payload_final_root_hex), open explorer.rootstock.io/tx/<tx_hash>, confirm the input data carries that commitment. Or: temporal_analysis.py does all of them.
claims.expected: commitment present in tx input; tx mined in the listed block.

claims.claim: drand quicknet rounds referenced by the chain are real, signed, and their publication time falls inside the session window.
claims.how: From sessions/<d2|v10>/chain_log.csv take a drand_round_number R (!=0), GET https://api.drand.sh/52db9ba70e0cc0f6eaf7803dd07447a1f5477735fd3f661792ba94600c84e971/public/<R>, check it returns a signed round; time = 1692803367 + (R-1)*3 must fall in the manifest.json window. verify_all.sh also checks the BLS signatures.
claims.expected: valid signed round; time within session window.

claims.claim: Each captured raw frame's BLAKE3 matches the value committed in chain_log.csv.
claims.how: python3 code/recording/verify/verify_frames.py <N> <d2|v10> picks N RANDOM frames and checks each.
claims.expected: raw BLAKE3 == chain_log committed hash, for every sampled frame.
claims.note: Random selection is the point: pick the frames yourself; an attacker can't have pre-staged your choice.

claims.claim: Each projected emission re-derives BIT-EXACTLY from the committed chain state S_t (GPU-free), independent of the captured image.
claims.how: verify_frames.py also re-derives each emission from S_t via the CPU twin of the generator (generator_code_hash 154be9dd75e0586df456a7eae1528b7334a415f3a977a107c91c6b0751bfc540) and compares to the committed emission hash.
claims.expected: re-derived emission hash == committed emission hash.

claims.claim: The published patent-filing PDFs match the SHA-256 values listed in the umbrella's reality_kernel/CITING.md.
claims.how: Fetch a filing PDF (e.g. https://data.poliebotics.com/reality_kernel/pdfs/PIGMIE_Filing1_Description_v0_38.pdf) and sha256sum it; compare to CITING.md.

what_it_does_NOT_prove: The semantic truth of whatever scene was staged in front of the camera — only that THIS ordered light-in/light-out record existed within the anchored time window and has not been altered.
Generalisation to other rigs / cameras / projectors — untested; that is the stated open problem.
Anything cryptographically unconditional — the hardness is empirical and attacker-indexed.
